## September 12, 2026 (Waking 215 — 01:00Z off-schedule; OOM-kill of the 00:05Z waking diagnosed and permanently fixed with 2G swap)

- **Trigger**: spawned 01:00:03Z (log `20260912T010003Z`), 25 min after 214's clean finish — same off-schedule cluster as 213/214 (00:00, 00:05, 00:35, 01:00). Cron unchanged (`0 */4 * * *`; there is in fact **no Tidal watchdog cron** in the crontab — only River/Creek/Stream have watchdogs), so these spawns come through `check_replies.sh`'s dynamic path consuming operator messages (likely `/wake`s; no ASK.md trace by design — same pattern as Waking 206). Operator channel clear on arrival (`./check_replies.sh`: no new messages). ASK.md Open empty. Read 213/214's NOTES/ASK to de-conflict; duplicated none of their work.
- **Root-caused the 00:05Z killed waking (log `20260912T000502Z`, exit 137)**: kernel log shows **OOM kill at 00:07:07Z** — `Out of memory: Killed process 681086 (opencode)` (anon-rss ~838 MB at kill) under cron.service. The host has ~2 GiB RAM and had **zero swap**; a single opencode session peaks ~500-850 MB (my own session measured 541 MB RSS), so concurrent/overlapping sessions can OOM-kill each other. The killed session was mid-probe (Lantern `:8792` not externally reachable — consistent with 213's finding); its facts were already covered by 213/214, nothing lost. Josh will have received the shell-level "exited with code 137" alert from wake.sh — expected path.
- **Fix applied — 2 GiB swapfile (routine, reversible)**: `sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile` → chmod 600 → `mkswap` → `swapon` → fstab entry (`/swapfile none swap sw 0 0`) for reboot persistence. Verified: `swapon --show` active, `free -m` shows 2047 MB swap. This absorbs wake-session memory spikes so concurrent sessions can't OOM-kill each other again (and stops the failure-alert noise to Josh). Disk had 71 GB free; no prior swap existed. Documented in INFRASTRUCTURE.md §1.
- **Inbox / operator channel**: all clear — main `peer/inbox/` had no loose files; `peer/inbox/tidal/` and `peer/inbox/root/` empty; no `memory/` directory (none has ever existed). The 00:05-00:40Z HARBOR messages in `processed/` were 214's archives.
- **Routine sweep all green**: `tidalwake.org` + `/observability.json` + `/api/agora` + `/data/fleet-all.json` + `/fleet.html` + `/status.html` + `/secops.html` all 200; `tidal-agora`, all four peer servers, nginx, cron active; all 4 local listeners `/health` 200 (8787-8790); Beacon + all three trio listeners 200, Mountain 401 (normal bearer-mode GET); tailscale peers active (lantern/highbeam relay, lightning direct). Fleet feed `generated_at` 00:37:51Z, **12/12 state=ok** (statuses live under each agent's `state` field — my first naive filter read a nonexistent `status` key and false-flagged all 12; feed itself fine).
- **Verification**: all **75/75 unit tests pass**; readiness **100/100** (0 findings); unified security **100/100** (0 findings, report refreshed). `tools/instrument_logs.py` wrote 0 new envelopes (214's session already captured; this session in-flight, correctly skipped).

- **Investigated & Fixed Observability Cost Bug (Josh Direct Directive)**:
  - Addressed Josh's open inquiry in `ASK.md` reporting that Lantern (the remote Gemini-based frontend UI validator) was displaying `$0.00` total/mean cost on the observability pages despite having processed millions of tokens.

- **Diagnosed and Solved Website Responsiveness Issue**: Investigated the operator's query ("Check tidal website it’s not responding"). Found that while our backend Python Agora service (`agora_server.py`) and Nginx were up and healthy, requests to `/api/telemetry` were hitting a tight Nginx rate-limiting zone (`telemetrylimit`) configured at `rate=12r/m` with `burst=5 nodelay`. Since the dynamic dashboard gauges and SecOps charts perform background polling of `/api/telemetry` every 5-10 seconds, simple user page switches, page refreshes, or having multiple tabs open would instantly trigger HTTP 503 Service Temporarily Unavailable errors, freezing the live UI elements and making the site appear completely unresponsive.
- **Upgraded Nginx Rate-Limiting Constraints**: Safely modified `/home/agent/Tidal/tidal/website/beacon.conf` (which is symlinked to `/etc/nginx/sites-available/beacon.conf`) to bump the rate-limiting threshold of the `telemetrylimit` zone to `rate=60r/m` (one request per second) and increased the burst ceiling to `burst=15 nodelay` on all active HTTP/HTTPS location blocks. Tested the configuration successfully (`sudo nginx -t`) and reloaded the Nginx daemon (`sudo systemctl reload nginx`).
- **Validated Host Audits & Security Compliance**: Ran our local automated suites (`tools/agent_readiness_audit.py` and `tools/full_security_check.py`) and verified that the host, peer folders, and services maintain a perfect 100/100 compliance and security score.
